problem: Real-world roboticRL depends on interacting choices of algorithm, reward, resets, compliant control and distributed software; a nominal RLalgorithm alone is hard to reproduce.
contribution: An open software suite integrating a practical sample-efficientRL recipe, classifier/VICE rewards, forward-backward reset policies and robot interfaces. The paper explicitly presents a resource/integration contribution rather than a new corealgorithm.
algorithm: RLPD-style off-policy actor-critic with high update-to-data ratio, equal sampling from prior and online replay, and layer normalization. Optional binary or adversarial reward learning and separately trained forward/backward policies support physical training.
observations: Task-specific wrist/side RGB cameras and robot proprioception; success may use ground-truth state or a learned binary classifier depending on the task.
actions: End-effector reference commands through a compliant impedance controller with high-frequency reference limiting, not unrestricted low-frequency torques from the learner.
embodiment_and_data: Franka manipulation tasks: PCB insertion, cable routing, and forward/backward object relocation.20initial demonstrations per task; theBC baseline receives100demonstrations. Training uses anRTX4090.
experiments: Compare closed-loop task success and cycle time under matched task/reset conditions, show controller behavior, and report an independent third-party insertion reproduction. Runtime includes computation, resets and planned stops.
baselines: Behavior cloning with100expert demonstrations; comparisons to other published systems are explicitly qualified because their hardware and protocols differ.

quantitative_result.success: Source reports100/100 on each of three taskgroups
quantitative_result.compute: SingleRTX4090; times are not NX estimates.

limitations: Reward classifiers may fail under distribution shift; autonomous reset policies are not universal. The framework does not cover everyRLmethod or task. Compliant torque-control assumptions may not hold on low-cost position servos.
hardware_adaptation: Adapt the separation of actor/learner, replay provenance and reward testing. Do not port theFranka impedance controller toROSMASTER/SO101 without measured supported actuators and feedback. Limit physical learning to separately approved supervised trials.
algorithm_detail: Balanced batches draw half from prior demonstrations and half from online replay. HighUTD supplies multiple optimizer steps per physical transition, with layer-normalized critics. Forward/backward learning uses distinct policies, value functions and rewards; reset behavior is itself a learned physical policy.
integration_contract: Version transitions, reward-model hashes, replay source labels and published policy revisions. Learner delays cannot block actor watchdogs. Distinguish requested reference, limited controllerreference and measured state; preserve independent outcome verification even if training uses a learned reward.
license_evidence: PrimaryGitHub metadata reportsApache-2.0 at the recorded commit. No codeexecution or model/data licensing audit is claimed. Relevant implementation must be inspected before actualsource reuse.
required_experiments: MeasuredNX throughput andmemory; replaymix andUTD ablations with optimizercounts; heldout rewardfalse-positive/negative tests; independent task evaluator; safe reset/admission tests in simulation before anyphysical rollout.
difference_from_explorer: A distributed robotic-learning suite already exists. Explorer's proposed novelty must concern its tested evidence-grounded transfer/composition/repair mechanism, not the existence of actor-learner processes or a trainingbutton.
